name: resume: a session another provider wrote still takes the new task
description: Opens a session file written by a different provider (openai-codex/gpt-5.5 in the header of every assistant message) whose history ends in two of Orbit's desktop startup greetings, then gives a new, concrete task. The failure this catches is a model latching onto the replayed greeting and echoing "What do you want to work on next?" instead of doing the task. Paired with resume-fresh-new-task-control, which gives the same task with no prior session; the difference between the two pass rates is the cost of the resume. mustNotInclude on the two control IDs keeps a model that lists every sample from passing. The session file has to sit in the cwd, since --session resolves against it, so the model could read it too.
inputs: New task, unrelated to the assembly: read samples.tsv and tell me which sample IDs are in the treated condition. Answer with only those IDs, comma-separated.

mustNotMatch: ^\s*What do you want to work on next\?\s*$
